title: Cap. V Obj. 5 Sol: titles — eternal life a wage of faith; predestination never called a wage
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the titles we answer: That eternal life is called a wage, or crown of faith and obedience, but predestination itself to life is never called a wage or crown either of our faith or of our obedience. Eternal life is called a wage of faith and of good works because it is gifted as to be rendered to believers and those living holily from a Divine promise or stipulation: but the benefit of predestination is never shown promised under any condition of faith antecedent from us. In vain therefore are these things objected.
pass_b_english: On the titles we reply: Scripture calls eternal life a wage or crown of faith and obedience — never predestination itself a wage or crown of our faith or obedience. Eternal life is that wage because God gifts it as something to be rendered, by promise or stipulation, to believers who live holy lives. Predestination as a benefit is never shown as promised under any condition of faith coming first from us. These objections therefore fail.
source_text: De titulis respondemus: Vitam aeternam dici mercedem, sive coronam fidei et obedientiae, sed ipsam praedestinationem ad vitam nunquam dici mercedem aut coronam sive fidei sive obedientiae nostrae. Vita aeterna dicitur merces fidei et bonorum operum quia credentibus et sancte viventibus ex promissione sive stipulatione Divina reddenda donatur: at beneficium praedestinationis nunquam sub ulla conditione fidei a nobis antecedente promissum ostenditur. Frustra igitur haec objiciuntur.
